usage: 한 달에 얼마나 벌어요?
How much do you make a month?
직장 동료끼리는 좀 민감하지만 친구 사이에선 흔히 묻는 질문
돈 벌려고 주말에도 알바해요.
I work a part-time job even on weekends to earn money.
돈(을) 벌다 = make money; 조사 을/를 는 회화에서 자주 생략
examples: 요즘 부업으로 용돈 좀 벌고 있어요.
These days I'm earning some pocket money with a side gig.
부업 = side job, 용돈 = spending money
고생해서 번 돈이니까 함부로 쓰지 마.
It's money you earned through hard work, so don't spend it carelessly.
번 = 벌다 의 관형형(과거), '벌은' 이 아님에 주의
주식으로 돈 벌기가 그렇게 쉬운 게 아니에요.
Making money from stocks isn't that easy.
-기가 쉽다/어렵다 패턴과 자주 결합
nuance: 벌다 is the everyday verb for earning or making money through work or income — 돈을 벌다 is the core phrase. It is a ㄹ-irregular verb: the final ㄹ drops before -ㅂ니다 and -니, giving 법니다, but stays in 벌어요. A very common trap is the past modifier form: 'the money I earned' is 번 돈, never 벌은 돈, because the ㄹ also drops before -ㄴ. Note 벌다 means to acquire income, while spending is 쓰다 and saving is 모으다.
mistakes: Saying 벌은 돈 for 'earned money' — the ㄹ drops before -ㄴ, so the correct modifier is 번 돈.

usage: 전셋집 구하려고 돈 모으고 있어요.
I'm saving up money to get a jeonse place.
전세 보증금 마련은 한국 2030 의 현실적인 저축 목표
우리 회비 좀 모아야 회식하지.
We need to collect the dues to have a team dinner.
돈을 모으다 = collect/pool money from people, not just personal saving
examples: 1년 동안 천만 원을 모았어요.
I saved up ten million won over a year.
목돈을 모으다 = build up a lump sum
적금 들어서 차근차근 모으는 중이에요.
I opened a savings account and I'm saving up little by little.
적금(을) 들다 = sign up for an installment savings account
동전 모아서 저금통 가득 채웠어요.
I gathered up coins and filled the piggy bank.
모으다 도 '한데 모으다'(gather) 의미로 두루 쓰임
nuance: 모으다 covers both saving money over time and gathering/pooling things or people together (돈, 동전, 사람, 자료). It is a ㅡ-irregular verb: the ㅡ drops before -아/어, and because the preceding vowel ㅗ is bright, it takes 아 — so 모으 + 아요 becomes 모아요, past 모았어요. Don't confuse it with 모이다, the intransitive pair ('to be gathered / people gather'): 사람들이 모여요. Saving is 모으다; the opposite, spending wastefully, is 낭비하다.
mistakes: Writing 모으어요 or 모워요 — as a ㅡ-irregular it becomes 모아요, and the past is 모았어요.

usage: 돈 좀 아껴 써.
Spend your money more sparingly.
아껴 쓰다 = use frugally; 가장 흔한 결합형
요즘 생활비 아끼느라 외식 거의 안 해요.
I barely eat out these days to save on living costs.
아끼다 = cut back / economize on a resource
examples: 전기 아끼려고 안 쓰는 콘센트는 다 뺐어요.
I unplugged all the unused outlets to save electricity.
돈뿐 아니라 전기·물·시간도 아끼다 의 대상이 됨
아낄 땐 아끼고 쓸 땐 써야죠.
You should save when you should save and spend when you should spend.
원어민이 자주 쓰는 균형 잡힌 소비 표현
택시비 아끼려고 그냥 걸어왔어요.
I just walked to save on the taxi fare.
-(으)려고 + 아끼다 로 절약 동기를 표현
nuance: 아끼다 means to be sparing with a resource so as not to waste it — money, electricity, water, even time. The set phrase 아껴 쓰다 ('use frugally') is extremely common. It also has a warmer second meaning, 'to treasure / cherish' a person or thing (아끼는 후배, 아끼는 옷). It conjugates regularly with ㅣ + 어 contracting to 여: 아끼 + 어요 becomes 아껴요, past 아꼈어요. Compare with 낭비하다, its direct opposite.
mistakes: Spelling the polite form 아끼어요 instead of contracting to 아껴요 (past 아꼈어요).

usage: 돈을 그렇게 낭비하면 안 돼.
You shouldn't waste money like that.
낭비하다 = squander; 부정적 뉘앙스가 강함
시간 낭비하지 말고 빨리 결정해.
Stop wasting time and decide quickly.
돈뿐 아니라 시간·돈·에너지를 낭비하다
examples: 충동구매로 돈 진짜 많이 낭비했어요.
I wasted so much money on impulse buys.
충동구매 = impulse purchase, 자주 함께 등장
이런 데 돈 낭비하느니 차라리 저금할래.
Rather than waste money on this, I'd rather save it.
-느니 차라리 = rather than ~, I'd rather
전기 낭비하는 거 보면 속상해요.
It upsets me to see electricity being wasted.
자원 낭비에도 두루 쓰임
nuance: 낭비하다 means to waste or squander a resource — money, time, energy — and always carries a clearly negative, wasteful tone. Because the 'please don't' meaning is what you actually say in daily life, both the polite command and the prohibitive collapse onto 낭비하지 마세요; a literal 낭비해 주세요 ('please waste it') would sound absurd. As a 하다 verb it conjugates regularly: 낭비해요, 낭비했어요, 낭비합니다. Its opposites are 아끼다 (be frugal) and 절약 (saving).
mistakes: Trying to use a polite-command 낭비해 주세요 — you never politely ask someone to waste; use the prohibitive 낭비하지 마세요.

usage: 빌린 돈 다음 달에 갚을게요.
I'll pay back the money I borrowed next month.
돈을 갚다 = repay money; -(으)ㄹ게요 로 약속
대출 다 갚으면 진짜 홀가분할 것 같아요.
I think I'll feel so relieved once I pay off the loan.
대출을 갚다 = pay off a loan
examples: 카드값 갚느라 이번 달은 텅장이에요.
I'm broke this month from paying off my credit card bill.
텅장 = '텅 빈 통장' (empty account) 슬랭
빚 다 갚고 나니까 마음이 편해요.
After paying off all my debt, I feel at ease.
빚을 갚다 = pay off debt
이 은혜 꼭 갚을게요.
I'll definitely repay this kindness.
은혜를 갚다 = repay a favor/kindness, 비유적 용법
nuance: 갚다 means to pay back what you owe — money (돈, 카드값, 대출, 빚) or, figuratively, a favor or kindness (은혜를 갚다). It is the natural counterpart to 빌리다 (to borrow). Despite ending in ㅍ it is fully regular: 갚 + 아요 becomes 갚아요, past 갚았어요, and the ㅍ stays in spelling though it sounds like [갑따]. Don't confuse 갚다 (pay back) with 값 (price), which is a noun.
mistakes: Dropping the final consonant in spelling (갚아요, not 가파요) even though it is pronounced [가파요].

usage: 돈은 은행에 맡기는 게 안전해요.
It's safer to deposit your money at the bank.
은행에 돈을 맡기다 = entrust/deposit money with a bank
짐 좀 프런트에 맡겨도 돼요?
Can I leave my bags at the front desk?
맡기다 = leave something in someone's care; 짐/세탁물/아이
examples: 적금은 만기까지 은행에 맡겨 둘 거예요.
I'll leave the savings deposited at the bank until maturity.
맡겨 두다 = leave entrusted; 만기 = maturity
계산은 저한테 맡기세요. 제가 쏠게요.
Leave the bill to me. It's on me.
쏘다 = treat/pay (slang); 맡기다 로 '내가 알아서 할게'
전문가한테 맡기는 게 마음이 놓여요.
I feel reassured leaving it to a professional.
사람에게 일을 맡기다 = entrust a task to someone
nuance: 맡기다 means to entrust or hand something over into someone's care — money to a bank (돈을 은행에 맡기다 = deposit), bags to a counter, dry cleaning to a shop, or a job to a person. It is the causative counterpart of 맡다 (to take charge of). It conjugates regularly with ㅣ + 어 contracting to 여: 맡기 + 어요 becomes 맡겨요, past 맡겼어요. For purely financial deposits you may also hear 예금하다, but 맡기다 is the warm, everyday word.
mistakes: Confusing 맡기다 (entrust to others) with 맡다 (take charge oneself) — you 맡겨 your money to the bank, the bank 맡아 keeps it.

usage: 시장에서는 흥정하는 재미가 있어요.
Haggling is part of the fun at traditional markets.
전통시장·중고거래에서 흥정이 자연스러움
중고로 살 때 좀 흥정해 봤어요.
I tried haggling a bit when buying it secondhand.
흥정하다 = negotiate over price back and forth
examples: 사장님이랑 흥정해서 만 원 깎았어요.
I haggled with the owner and knocked off ten thousand won.
흥정하다 로 협상하고 깎다 로 결과를 표현
백화점에서는 흥정 안 통해요.
Haggling doesn't work at department stores.
정찰제 매장에선 흥정이 불가능함을 알려주는 표현
중고차 살 때 가격 흥정 꼭 하세요.
Make sure to negotiate the price when buying a used car.
가격을 흥정하다 = bargain over the price
nuance: 흥정하다 is to bargain or negotiate over a price, going back and forth until both sides agree — natural at traditional markets, in secondhand deals (중고거래), and for big buys like a used car. It describes the whole negotiation, whereas 깎다 is the concrete act of getting the price knocked down. Note that fixed-price stores (정찰제) like department stores or franchises don't allow it: 흥정 안 돼요. As a 하다 verb it is regular: 흥정해요, 흥정했어요.
mistakes: Treating 흥정하다 and 깎다 as identical — 흥정하다 is the negotiating process, 깎다 is actually lowering the price.

usage: 모자라는 돈은 제가 보탤게요.
I'll chip in the money that's short.
모자란 금액을 보태다 = add to make up a shortfall
생활비에 보태려고 부업 시작했어요.
I started a side job to help with living expenses.
-에 보태다 = put toward / contribute to
examples: 부모님이 결혼자금 좀 보태 주셨어요.
My parents chipped in some money for the wedding.
큰돈을 마련할 때 가족이 보태 주는 상황
선물값 다 같이 조금씩 보태자.
Let's all chip in a little for the gift.
보태다 = each person adds a small amount toward a total
용돈에 보태 쓰라고 십만 원 줬어요.
I gave 100,000 won to add to her allowance.
-에 보태 쓰다 = use as a supplement to
nuance: 보태다 means to add money or resources to make up a shortfall or supplement an amount — chipping in for a shared gift, helping with living costs, topping up someone's allowance. The pattern is 'X에 보태다' (put toward X). It differs from 모으다 (collect/pool a total): you 보태 your share into a pot that everyone 모아 together. It is a regular ㅐ-stem verb, so 보태 + 어요 stays 보태요, and the past contracts to 보탰어요.
mistakes: Writing the past tense as 보태었어요 — the stem vowel ㅐ absorbs 었, giving 보탰어요.

usage: 월급에서 세금을 떼고 줘요.
They take out taxes from the salary before paying.
월급에서 세금을 떼다 = deduct tax from pay
수수료 떼면 실제로 받는 건 더 적어요.
After they take the fee, what you actually get is less.
수수료를 떼다 = take a commission/fee out
examples: 주민센터에서 등본 한 통 뗐어요.
I got a copy of my residence registration at the community center.
서류를 떼다 = issue/obtain an official document (관용 표현)
중개수수료를 너무 많이 떼는 거 아니에요?
Aren't they taking too much in brokerage fees?
부동산 거래에서 자주 겪는 상황
선금으로 십만 원 먼저 떼 놨어요.
I set aside 100,000 won upfront as a deposit.
떼 놓다 = set apart / earmark an amount
nuance: 떼다 in a money context means to take a portion out — deducting tax or a fee from a larger sum (월급에서 세금을 떼다, 수수료를 떼다). It also has a very useful idiomatic sense: 서류를 떼다 means to obtain or issue an official document (등본, 초본) from an office, which residents do constantly. Literally it means to detach/peel something off. It is a regular ㅔ-stem verb: 떼 + 어요 stays 떼요, but the past contracts to 뗐어요.
mistakes: Writing the past as 떼었어요 — the ㅔ stem contracts with 었 to give 뗐어요.

usage: 부모님께 생활비를 부쳐 드려요.
I send living expenses to my parents.
돈을 부치다 = remit/send money (계좌로도, 송금 의미)
이 소포 미국으로 부치려고요.
I'd like to send this parcel to the US.
소포/편지를 부치다 = mail a parcel/letter at the post office
examples: 택배 말고 우체국에서 부쳤어요.
I sent it from the post office, not by courier.
우체국에서 부치다 = send via the post office
급해서 돈 먼저 부쳤으니까 확인해 봐.
I sent the money first since it's urgent, so check.
계좌로 돈을 부치다 = wire money to an account
등기로 부쳐 주세요.
Please send it by registered mail.
등기(우편) = registered mail; 우체국 필수 표현
nuance: 부치다 means to send something off to a distant place — a parcel or letter through the post office, or money to someone (돈을 부치다 = remit). For money it overlaps with 송금하다 / 보내다 but feels warmer and more everyday, especially family sending support. It conjugates regularly with ㅣ + 어 contracting to 여: 부치 + 어요 becomes 부쳐요, past 부쳤어요. Beware the homophone 붙이다 ('to stick/attach'), which is spelled differently though pronounced the same.
mistakes: Mixing up 부치다 (send/mail) with 붙이다 (stick on) — they sound identical but mean opposite things; 우표를 붙여서 편지를 부쳐요.

usage: 계좌번호 주시면 바로 송금할게요.
If you give me the account number, I'll transfer it right away.
계좌로 송금하다 = transfer to a bank account
해외 송금하는데 수수료가 꽤 비싸요.
International transfers have pretty high fees.
해외 송금 = overseas remittance, 외국인 거주자에게 중요
examples: 월세 송금했는데 입금 확인 좀 해 주세요.
I transferred the rent — please confirm you received it.
월세를 송금하다 = wire the monthly rent
앱으로 송금하면 1초도 안 걸려요.
Transferring through the app takes less than a second.
토스·카카오뱅크 등 모바일 송금이 일상화됨
잘못된 계좌로 송금했어요. 어떡하죠?
I transferred to the wrong account. What should I do?
착오송금 상황에서 쓰는 표현
nuance: 송금하다 is the precise banking word for transferring money from one account to another, used on bank apps, for paying rent, and for overseas remittances (해외 송금). It is more formal and account-specific than 부치다 or the casual 쏘다. In spoken Korean people also say 돈(을) 보내다 for the same thing. As a 하다 verb it is regular: 송금해요, 송금했어요, 송금합니다. The matching noun 송금 (remittance) appears on every banking screen.
mistakes: Pairing it with the wrong particle — money goes 계좌로/에게 송금하다 (to an account/person); the recipient is not marked with 을/를.

usage: 조금만 깎아 주세요.
Please knock the price down a little.
값을 깎아 달라 = the standard line for asking a discount
현금으로 내면 깎아 줘요?
Will you give a discount if I pay cash?
현금가 흥정 시 흔한 질문
examples: 사장님이 오천 원 깎아 주셨어요.
The owner knocked five thousand won off for me.
값을 깎다 = lower the price (seller's side: 깎아 주다)
중고로 사면서 가격 좀 깎았어요.
I got the price down a bit buying it secondhand.
중고거래에서 깎다 가 자연스러움
사과 깎아 먹을래?
Want me to peel an apple for you?
깎다 의 또 다른 뜻: 과일·연필을 깎다 (to peel/sharpen)
nuance: 깎다 in a money context means to knock down or discount a price — 값을 깎다 ('lower the price'), with the seller's 깎아 주다 ('give a discount') being the phrase you hear and use most. It is the concrete result of 흥정하다 (the negotiating). Outside money, 깎다 also means to peel or pare (과일을 깎다) and to sharpen (연필을 깎다). Despite ending in the double consonant ㄲ it is fully regular: 깎 + 아요 becomes 깎아요, past 깎았어요.
mistakes: Reducing the spelling to 까다/까아요 — keep the double ㄲ: 깎아요, 깎았어요 (pronounced [까까요]/[까깠어요]).
